blocks.text: The questions below come up in almost every Docker screen; each answer is the crisp version to say out loud.

rows: Container vs VM?
Process with namespaces + cgroups on the shared host kernel vs hardware virtualization with its own kernel; containers win on density and startup, VMs on isolation
Image vs container?
Immutable layered filesystem + config (by digest) vs an instance with a writable layer and runtime config
CMD vs ENTRYPOINT?
ENTRYPOINT = executable; CMD = default args; run args replace CMD; use exec form for signals
COPY vs ADD?
ADD also fetches URLs and auto-extracts tars; prefer COPY
ARG vs ENV?
ARG build-only (visible in history if used in RUN); ENV persists; neither for secrets
Layer caching?
Same parent + same instruction/content = hit; first miss rebuilds the rest; dependencies before source
Smaller images?
Slim base, multi-stage, same-layer cleanup, .dockerignore, CPU-only wheels
Volume vs bind mount?
Docker-managed, portable, pre-populated vs a host path for dev source and config
Container communication?
User-defined network, service name, container port; default bridge has no DNS
EXPOSE vs -p?
Metadata vs host mapping on 0.0.0.0 by default
Exits immediately?
PID 1 ended: finished, daemonized, or crashed; check logs and exit code
Exit 137?
SIGKILL: OOM, docker kill, or grace period expired
PID 1 problem?
Ignores unhandled signals, must reap zombies; exec form + exec "$@" + tini
depends_on waits?
No: use service_healthy plus app retries
Secrets?
Build: BuildKit secret mounts. Runtime: mounted files/secret manager; never ENV/ARG/COPY
Root in container safe?
Reduced root, still UID 0 on the host kernel; non-root USER, cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, read-only

blocks.text: Q: "What happens during docker run?" A: "The CLI calls dockerd's API; the image is pulled if missing; the container is created with a writable layer, config, mounts and a network endpoint; containerd starts a shim and runc sets up namespaces, cgroups and the rootfs and execs the entrypoint; then output is attached, or the ID is printed with -d."

items: Signals, layers and networking dominate screens.
Always name the fix, not just the cause.
Secrets and root questions test security judgment.
